teaser: He drew the helmet rings out of the Prophet's ﷺ cheek with his teeth, and lost the teeth doing it.
quran_mention: «إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا» — 'when he said to his companion, do not grieve, Allah is with us' (at-Tawbah 9:40). Offered leadership of the ummah, Abu Ubaydah refused with a reference to this verse: do you come to me while the third of three is among you.

layers.title: Who He Was
layers.subtitle: A tall, stooped man with broken front teeth
layers.content:
His name was Amir. Almost nobody used it. He was Amir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah ibn Hilal ibn Uhayb, of Banu al-Harith ibn Fihr of Quraysh, and history knows him by his kunya alone. His mother was Umayma bint Ghanm.

Malik ibn Yukhamir, who saw him, described a thin man with a veined face and a slight beard, tall, stooped in the back, with his front teeth broken. He dyed his head and beard with henna and katam. How the teeth were lost is the most famous thing about him, and he lost them on purpose.

On his ring he had five words cut: the fifth belongs to Allah. It is a line about public money — the share of war gains that is not the commander's to touch. He wore the rule where he could see it, on the hand that would be signing for it. He later governed Syria and had armies and treasuries under him, and he kept wearing it.

He had two sons, Yazid and Umayr. Ibn Sa'd notes plainly that the children of Abu Ubaydah died out and he has no descendants.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: Muslim before there was a room to meet in
layers.content:
Yazid ibn Ruman reports that Abu Ubaydah became Muslim together with Uthman ibn Maz'un, Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf and their companions before the Prophet ﷺ entered the house of al-Arqam. That house is where the first Muslims later gathered in secret. Abu Ubaydah was in before there was anywhere to gather.

Reports differ on whether he was among those who crossed to Abyssinia. Ibn Ishaq and al-Waqidi place him in the second migration; Musa ibn Uqba and Abu Ma'shar do not mention him in it.

When he emigrated to Madinah he lodged with Kulthum ibn al-Hidm. Then the Prophet ﷺ joined him in brotherhood — and the man he was joined to was Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfa. A man of Quraysh, tied for life to a former slave, and the sources record no comment about it from either of them. Another report names Muhammad ibn Maslama of the Ansar instead.

He fought at Badr at the age of forty-one, older than most of the men standing with him.
layers.source: Reported from Yazid ibn Ruman and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: The helmet at Uhud, the whale on the shore
layers.content:
Aisha heard Abu Bakr tell it. At Uhud two rings of the Prophet's ﷺ iron helmet had driven into his cheek. Abu Bakr reached for them and Abu Ubaydah stopped him: I ask you by Allah, let me. He gripped one ring in his teeth and drew it out slowly so as not to tear the wound further, and went over backwards, and his front tooth came away with it. Then he asked for the second, and did it again, and lost the other. That is why the man is described in the books as broken-toothed.

The Prophet ﷺ later sent him down the coast with a little over three hundred men. Their rations came down to a handful of dates each, then one date each, then leaves boiled in pots and strained — which is why they were called the army of Khabat, the army of leaves. On the shore they found a dead whale. Abu Ubaydah's first ruling was that it was carrion and they would not eat. Then he said: this is the army of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the way of Allah, and we are in need. They ate for a fortnight. Thirteen men sat inside its eye-socket.
layers.hadith_ref: The Uhud account — reported from Aisha from Abu Bakr, Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III; also al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, citing Ibn Hibban. The Khabat expedition — narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah, Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: Offered the ummah, and he said no
layers.content:
The people of Yemen asked the Prophet ﷺ to send them a man to teach them. He took Abu Ubaydah's hand and said: this is the trusty one of this nation. To a delegation from Najran asking for a trustworthy man he answered that he would send them one truly trustworthy, and repeated the phrase three times before choosing him.

Then the Prophet ﷺ died, and the title was tested. Umar came to Abu Ubaydah and said: stretch out your hand and I will give you allegiance — you are the trustworthy one of this community on the tongue of the Messenger of Allah. Abu Ubaydah's answer was a rebuke wrapped in respect: I have never seen a weakness in you since you became Muslim. Will you pledge to me while the Siddiq is among you, the second of two? In another wording: do you come to me while the third of three is here.

As governor of Syria he told the people from the pulpit that he was a man of Quraysh, and that there was no one among them, red or black, with more taqwa than him without his wishing he could be inside that man's skin.
layers.hadith_ref: 'Every nation has a trustee, and the trustee of this nation is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah' — narrated by Anas ibn Malik, Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: He would not leave a city that was dying
layers.content:
Umar tested him once with money: four thousand dirhams and four hundred dinars, and instructions to the courier to watch what he did with it. He gave all of it away. Umar sent the same to Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who gave away everything except what his wife said the house needed, and Umar said: praise be to Allah, who has put people like this into Islam.

In 17 AH Umar was riding towards Syria and turned back at Sargh on news of plague. Abu Ubaydah asked him: do you flee from the decree of Allah? Umar answered: no — to the decree of Allah. The next year the plague of Amwas swept Syria and Abu Ubaydah stayed with his army in it. When it took him he appointed Mu'adh over the troops. Irbad ibn as-Sariya visited him dying and heard him say, may Allah forgive Umar for turning back from Sargh, and then narrate that whoever dies of the plague is a martyr.

He died in 18 AH at fifty-eight. Umar said afterwards that had Abu Ubaydah lived, he would have made him caliph — and told Allah he had only followed His Prophet's word about the man.
layers.hadith_ref: 'The one who dies of the plague is a martyr' — narrated by Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah to Irbad ibn as-Sariya, Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

quiz.prompt: How did Abu Ubaydah lose his front teeth?

options.text: A blow from a sword at Badr
Pulling the rings of the Prophet's ﷺ helmet out of his cheek with his teeth
A fall from his camel at Tabuk
Illness in his old age

quiz.citation: Reported from Aisha from Abu Bakr — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III; also al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, citing Ibn Hibban
quiz.scholar_reflection: He asked Abu Bakr twice to be allowed to do it, once for each ring. He pulled slowly so as not to worsen the wound, and paid a tooth each time.

quiz.prompt: What title did the Prophet ﷺ give Abu Ubaydah when the people of Yemen asked for a teacher?

options.text: The sword of Allah
The trusty one of this nation
The reciter of this nation
The disciple of the Prophet ﷺ

quiz.citation: Narrated by Anas ibn Malik — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He took Abu Ubaydah by the hand while he said it. To Najran he promised a trustworthy man and repeated the word three times before naming him.

quiz.prompt: Why was the expedition Abu Ubaydah led down the coast called the army of Khabat?

options.text: It marched at night
It carried no weapons
Khabat means leaves, which they boiled and strained to drink when the dates ran out
It was named after a valley

quiz.citation: Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Rations went from a handful of dates each, to one date each, to leaves. Then they found a dead whale on the shore, and thirteen men sat inside its eye-socket.

quiz.prompt: What did Abu Ubaydah do when Umar offered him allegiance as leader after the Prophet ﷺ died?

options.text: He accepted and then resigned
He asked for time to consult the Ansar
He refused, asking how he could be pledged to while Abu Bakr was there
He proposed Ali instead

quiz.citation: Reported from Ibrahim at-Taymi — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He called Abu Bakr the Siddiq and the second of two, and in another wording the third of three — a reference to the two in the cave in Surah at-Tawbah.

quiz.prompt: What did Abu Ubaydah say to Umar when Umar turned back at Sargh on hearing of the plague?

options.text: Nothing — he agreed with the decision
'Do you flee from the decree of Allah?'
That the army would follow him back
That he should send Khalid instead

quiz.scholar_reflection: Umar answered: no, to the decree of Allah. Abu Ubaydah stayed in Syria, died in the plague of Amwas the following year, and on his deathbed asked Allah to forgive Umar for turning back.

quiz.prompt: Abu Ubaydah wore a reminder about public money on his ring, where he would see it every day. What rule do you need in front of your eyes to keep?

options.text: Something about money
Something about my temper or my tongue
Something about prayer or time
I rely on remembering, and often do not

quiz.citation: Reported from Qatada on the engraving of Abu Ubaydah's ring — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He governed Syria with treasuries under him and kept wearing it. He did not assume that knowing the rule was the same as keeping it.

quiz.prompt: He was pledged the leadership of the ummah and turned it down. What have you been offered that you knew you should not take?
quiz.slider_label: Turning down what you could have

options.text: A position I was not right for
Money or work that came with a cost
Praise I had not earned
Nothing — I take what is offered

quiz.citation: Reflection on the account of Ibrahim at-Taymi — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He did not say he was unworthy. He said someone else was more entitled and named him. Refusal is easier when you can point at the right answer.

quiz.prompt: Facing starving men, he changed his own ruling on the whale from no to yes. How do you handle discovering you were wrong in front of people who followed you?

options.text: Say it plainly and move on
Quietly change course without naming it
Hold the line to protect my authority
It depends who is watching

quiz.citation: Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He gave a reason rather than a retraction: this is the army of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the way of Allah, and we are in need. The Prophet ﷺ afterwards called it provision Allah had sent them.

quiz.prompt: He told the people of Syria he wished he could be inside the skin of anyone among them with more taqwa. What does your standing in others' eyes do to you?

options.text: It steadies me — I try to deserve it
It weighs on me more than it helps
I enjoy it and know I should not
I do not think anyone holds one of me

quiz.citation: Reported from Thabit — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He said it as governor, from a position where nobody could contradict him. He also once said he wished he were a ram, so that his people could slaughter him and eat.

quiz.prompt: He stayed in a province that was dying of plague, and died in it. What would keep you somewhere costly rather than leaving?

options.text: People who depend on me
A duty I accepted and will not drop
Nothing — I would protect my family first
I honestly do not know until it happens

quiz.citation: Reflection on the plague of Amwas, 18 AH — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: There is no simple lesson here. Umar left on the news and Abu Ubaydah questioned him for it, then died asking Allah to forgive him. Both men were doing their duty as they saw it.
